title: Smaller UPI Apps Urge NPCI to Rethink UPI Meta Launch, Cite Risk of Deeper Market Concentration
excerpt: A coalition of payment firms including Paytm and CRED has written to India's payments authority opposing a one-click checkout framework they say could permanently entrench PhonePe and Google Pay's dominance.
body:
• Several UPI apps including Paytm, CRED, and Flipkart's Super.money have jointly urged NPCI to halt the rollout of UPI Meta, a proposed one-click checkout framework
  • The companies argue the system would lock users into their current default UPI app at onboarding, giving PhonePe and Google Pay — which together control roughly 78% of transactions — a structural advantage
  • NPCI had been targeting a launch around the Global Fintech Fest later this year, partly to compete with Apple Pay's expected entry into India
  • The firms are calling for broader industry consultation before implementation, warning there is no evidence the current checkout process causes meaningful transaction drop-offs

Coalition Pushes Back on NPCI Proposal

A group of smaller digital payment firms has written to the National Payments Corporation of India opposing the planned rollout of UPI Meta, a tokenisation framework that would let users save their preferred UPI application on merchant platforms for one-click checkouts.

https://x.com/chandrarsrikant/status/2080271863176163538

In a joint letter dated July 23, reviewed by Reuters, the companies — which include Paytm, Meta-backed CRED, and Flipkart's Super.money — told NPCI the proposal could "adversely impact" competition in India's digital payments ecosystem.

Under the proposed system, also referred to as UPI Checkout, users would save a preferred payment handle or linked bank account with merchants such as Amazon, Blinkit, and Swiggy. Instead of being redirected to a UPI app for every purchase, they would authenticate directly on the merchant platform using a PIN or biometric, similar to tokenised card transactions.

"The proposed framework is expected to materially increase persistence of customer preference towards the [third-party apps] selected during the initial setup process."

— Joint industry letter to NPCI, July 23

Why Incumbents Stand to Gain

At the heart of the opposition is a simple behavioural argument: default settings rarely change. Once a consumer selects a UPI app during onboarding on a merchant platform, the smaller firms contend, that choice is likely to persist indefinitely — and the app most likely to be selected first is the one already installed on the most phones.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=8OTfmLsLrJM

The numbers make the incumbents' advantage stark. PhonePe accounts for roughly 45% of UPI transaction volume, according to the latest industry data reported by BusinessLine. Google Pay holds about 33%. Together, they process nearly four-fifths of all UPI transactions. Smaller apps — Navi, Super.money, BHIM — each handle around 1-2% of volume.

"Over time, this may create structural advantages for larger incumbent apps with significant existing customer bases, while making customer acquisition and transaction share growth increasingly challenging for smaller and emerging UPI apps," the representation noted, according to BusinessLine.

The companies also argued that the proposal addresses a problem that does not exist. Unlike card tokenisation, which replaces the need to repeatedly enter card details, UPI already provides a largely frictionless payment experience. No ecosystem-wide evidence has been presented showing that the current checkout process causes material customer drop-offs or transaction abandonment, the letter stated.

Timing and Competitive Context

NPCI had been targeting a launch around the Global Fintech Fest later this year. The push to streamline UPI checkout comes partly in anticipation of Apple Pay's expected entry into the Indian market, which would add another major competitor to the ecosystem.

UPI processed over 227 billion transactions worth more than 28 trillion rupees ($290 billion) in June alone, making it one of the world's most widely used fast payment networks, according to NPCI data cited by Reuters.

The debate over market concentration is not new. NPCI introduced a plan in 2020 to cap any single UPI app's market share at 30%, but has repeatedly delayed enforcement. The current compliance deadline is December 2026. Meanwhile, the combined share of PhonePe and Google Pay recently dipped below 80% for the first time — to 79% in May 2026 — as smaller apps including Navi, Super.money, and WhatsApp Pay gained ground.

"We respectfully request NPCI to undertake broader consultation with third-party application providers and other ecosystem participants and comprehensively evaluate the concerns highlighted above before progressing with the proposed framework."

— Joint industry representation to NPCI

What It Means for Users Abroad

For members of the Indian diaspora who use UPI for cross-border remittances or payments to family and merchants in India, the framework could have practical implications. A one-click system tied to a single saved UPI app could limit flexibility for users who switch between platforms or use different apps for different purposes — a pattern common among NRIs managing payments across geographies.

What Comes Next

NPCI and the signatory companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment, according to Reuters. The payments authority now faces a decision: proceed with a framework that could modernise checkout but risk entrenching a duopoly, or slow the rollout for broader consultation as the industry demands. With the 30% market share cap deadline approaching in December and Apple Pay looming, the stakes for India's $290-billion digital payments market have rarely been higher.
nri_angle: NRIs using UPI for cross-border remittances and payments to family in India could face reduced flexibility if a one-click checkout system locks users into a single default payment app.
